correctness.rationale: The proof uses the established isomorphism of the face algebra with the path algebra of the synchronous square, with acyclicity preserved. Parallel arrows produce four parallel square arrows and wild type; otherwise squared local in/out degrees identify all wild high-degree cases. The remaining fork produces affine D4 and every proper connected enlargement is wild by strict adjacency-spectral-radius monotonicity. Complete ordered pairs of directed paths/forks yield only type A, affine D4 and affine A3 components, proving necessity, sufficiency, and exact multiplicities. The finite-type interval indecomposable count equals the square-path count. The included NumPy checker matched 857 finite acyclic instances; no inference from sampling to the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The source theorem determines the square path algebra for every input and classical Gabriel/affine classification determines representation type once that square has been analyzed; these powerful prior reductions are credited. The new claim is the nontrivial global characterization of which original quivers yield finite/tame/wild square components, the exact fork-pair affine-factor multiplicities, and the finite indecomposable identity. Complete accessible source sections and relevant returned records did not explicitly state or imply this sharp component criterion without the new combinatorial branching/enlargement argument.
residual_risks: The classical graph representation classification plus the universal face-algebra isomorphism gives an algorithmic determination for every input; another author may already have published the explicit input-level simplification.

value.rationale: Finite/tame/wild representation type is a foundational invariant of face algebras. The exact decision criterion is stated directly on a source quiver instead of requiring construction/classification of a quadratically larger square. The f-squared affine component count identifies all parameter-family factors, and the finite-case equality between indecomposable isoclasses and algebra dimension is a natural exact invariant. The threshold at the isolated two-arrow fork is sharp and nontrivial; it is not a table recomputation or arbitrary finite slice.
